Eﬀect of nano-bubble water on high solid anaerobic digestion of pig manure:
Focus on digestion stability, methanogenesis performance and related
mechanisms
Yujie Fana, Zhongfang Leib, Xiaojing Yanga, Motoyoshi Kobayashib, Yasuhisa Adachib,
Zhenya Zhangb, Kazuya Shimizub,⁎
a Graduate School of Life and Environmental Sciences, University of Tsukuba, 1-1-1 Tennodai, Tsukuba, Ibaraki 305-8572, Japan
b Faculty of Life and Environmental Sciences, University of Tsukuba, 1-1-1 Tennodai, Tsukuba, Ibaraki 305-8572, Japan
A R T I C L E I N F O
Keywords:
Anaerobic digestion
Nano-bubble water
Pig manure
Digestion stability
Methanogenesis performance
A B S T R A C T
In this study, high solid anaerobic digestion of pig manure (PM) under nano-bubble water (NBW) addition was
investigated with focus on digestion stability, methanogenesis performance and related mechanisms. Volatile
fatty acids (VFAs) inhibition occurred when total solids (TS) was about 8% without NBW addition, which was
alleviated with improved digestion stability under NBW addition, facilitating the process of high solids anaerobic
digestion (HSAD). The cumulative CH4 yield, on the other hand, was 201–230 mL/g-VS in the NBW reactors at
TS of 3–6%, about 20.3–25.0% higher than the control reactors. At the same time, with higher water mobility
and zeta potential, NBW was found to promote the consumption of soluble proteins/carbohydrates during the
above AD process.
1. Introduction
The amount of pig manure (PM) produced in Japan is approxi-
mately 21 million tons per year (MAFF, 2019). Animal manure is
generally treated by using wet anaerobic digestion (AD) which has been
applied in the processing of livestock manure due to its many ad-
vantages (Kothari et al., 2014). The advantages of wet AD as a con-
ventional method to treat animal manure has been less susceptible to
inhibition and shorter lag phase, especially. However, wet AD still has
many shortcomings when dealing with livestock manure including
water-wasting, inconvenient operation, low energy recovery, and low
fermentation slurry concentration (Chen et al., 2015). Therefore, in
terms of economy and operability, it is necessary to ﬁnd a more cost-
eﬀective and easy-to-operate method.
In comparison to wet AD with total solids (TS) 2–6%, high solids
anaerobic digestion (HSAD), which often refers to AD with TS content
higher than 8%, could be applied with more biogas production and less
heat consumption (Liao and Li, 2015). The economic beneﬁts of HSAD
include not only the CH4 produced from the AD process but also the
digestate with the potential for fertilizer. HSAD, as an outstanding AD
technology, has been widely used to treat various waste, such as
chicken manure (Sun et al., 2016), dairy manure (Saady and Massé,
2015), pig manure (Huang et al., 2016; Wu et al., 2017), sewage sludge
(Liu et al., 2016). However, it has some shortcomings, such as being
susceptible to inhibition and longer lag phase (Chen et al., 2014). In
addition, the high nitrogen content in PM could accumulate a large
amount of ammonia nitrogen leading to cause ammonia inhibition in
the AD process. The volatile solids (VS) removal rate of HSAD is also
lower than that of conventional wet AD. Moreover, as the TS content
increased, the mass transfer eﬃciency of the fermentation in the di-
gester decreased and the rheological behavior of the digestates will be
strongly aﬀected, which adversely aﬀected the use of the substrates by
the microorganism (Garcia-Bernet et al., 2011). The microbial activity
was also signiﬁcantly reduced relative to wet AD (Liu et al., 2016).
Many methods can be used to improve HSAD performance such as
thermal hydrolysis process (Xue et al., 2015), percolate recirculation
technology (Rico et al., 2015), continuous plug-ﬂow dry AD reactor
technology (Chen et al. 2015), low-temperature hydrothermal pre-
treatment (Huang et al., 2017). However, due to chemicals pollution
and energy consumption or complicated operation, most of these
methods have not been applied in industry. Although co-digestion can
eﬀectively avoid inhibition in HSAD process, it needs to add additional
substrates with high C/N ratio, which increases the complexity of the
operation and reduces the PM treatment capacity.
Water plays a very important role in the AD process because water
promotes substrate hydrolysis and transfers the hydrolysate and other

intermediates to the sites where the microorganisms can be utilized
(Kothari et al., 2014). Nano-bubble water (NBW) has a large amount of
nanoscale particle bubbles. Since nanobubbles have characteristics of
great pressure, large speciﬁc surface area and minimal diameter, NBW
has properties that are not possessed by ordinary water, such as strong
adsorption, high air solubility, long storage time, etc. (Liu et al., 2019).
Due to its unique characteristics, NBW has important value in the ﬁelds
of industry (Kim et al., 2020), agricultural water management (Zhou
et al., 2019), medicine (Hayashi et al., 2019), environmental pollution
control (Xiao et al., 2019) and so on. One recent work showed that
methane production was increased by 29% from waste activated sludge
in AD process under N2-nanobubble water addition (Yang et al., 2019).
This work indicates that adding NBW has a positive eﬀect in AD process
to recover methane, but so far, few reports have been found to apply
NBW in HSAD. Whether NBW can eﬀectively avoid the shortcomings
such as inhibition in the HSAD process is still unknown.
The aim of this research was to investigate the eﬀect of NBW on
HSAD, and to reveal a new path to enhance methane production and
digestion stability of HSAD rather than using conventional methods. In
order to evaluate the digestion stability of HSAD, this study measured
the pH value, total alkalinity (TA), total ammonia nitrogen (TAN) and
volatile fatty acids (VFAs). In addition, soluble organics in HSAD were
also determined to assess HSAD performance. This work was the ﬁrst
study to reveal the eﬀects of adding NBW on digestion stability, me-
thanogenesis performance and the related mechanisms in the HSAD
process of PM.
2. Materials and methods
2.1. Batch anaerobic fermentation experiments
2.1.1. Raw manure and seed AD sludge
In this study, fresh PM was sampled from the domestic pig farm in
Tsukuba, Ibaraki, Japan. The manure sample was collected manually to
remove large particles. Then, the raw PM was stored at 4 °C. In this
research, digested sludge was collected from a wastewater treatment
plant located in Ibaraki, Japan, and then cultivated with the raw PM for
acclimation of inoculum. Table 1 shows the main characteristics of
inoculum and PM based on ﬁve tests in parallel.
2.1.2. Batch AD experiments
Batch AD tests were carried out using two kinds of glass bottles. The
500 mL Scott Duran bottles were used for preparation and acclimation
of inoculum and the 250 mL ones were applied for anaerobic digestion.
The digested sludge was cultivated with the raw PM ﬁrst under meso-
philic condition (35 ± 2 °C) for about one month. And then the di-
gestate was used as inoculum for the subsequent AD process. Four kinds
of experimental reactors were set up: R(3% TS)Control and R(3% TS)NBW
were loaded with 11 g PM + 89 g inoculum; R(6% TS)Control and R(6%
TS)NBW were loaded with 25 g PM + 75 g inoculum; R(8% TS)Control
and R(8% TS)NBW were loaded with 36 g PM + 64 g inoculum; R(10%
TS)Control and R(10% TS)NBW were loaded with 46 g PM + 54 g in-
oculum. At the beginning of the experiments, 100 mL NBW was added
into RNBW while 100 mL deionized water (DW) was added into RControl
(Table 2). Additionally, four bottles loaded with inoculum (89 g, 75 g,
64 g, and 54 g, respectively) only were also tested in this work corre-
sponding to four sets of experimental reactors. Biogas/methane pro-
duction used in this research was obtained by subtracting the amount
produced by the inoculum. To avoid microenvironment changes and to
simplify this AD processes that might be applied in practice, in this
study, no pH adjustment was conducted. All reactors were sealed with
aluminum caps and rubber stoppers. Before placed in a temperature-
controlled incubator (35 ± 2 °C), all the reactors were ﬂushed with
nitrogen gas for 2 min. After all reactors no longer produce gas for 4
consecutive days, the reaction stops. The reactors of R(3% TS)Control and
R(3% TS)NBW were carried out for 36 days, while that of R(6% TS)Control
and R(6% TS)NBW were 58 days. The reactors of R(8% TS)NBW were
carried out for 68 days. Although R(8% TS)Control, R(10% TS)Control and
R(10% TS)NBW no longer produce gas in late HSAD process, for com-
parison with R(8% TS)NBW, R(8% TS)Control were also carried out for
68 days. R(10% TS)Control and R(10% TS)NBW were conducted for
58 days. Each experiment was performed in duplicate. Shake all 250 mL
anaerobic digesters manually for 2 min every day at a ﬁxed time.
2.2. Preparation of NBW
NBW was prepared by a nano-bubble generator (HACK FB11,
JAPAN) according to the previous report (Wang et al., 2019). In-
troduced carbon dioxide gas into deionized water (DW) through this
generator at 20 ± 2 °C for 20 min to get NBW used throughout the AD
process in this research. During the preparation of NBW, the pressure
was controlled at 0.25 MPa and the ﬂow rates of DW and carbon di-
oxide gas were kept at 8 L/min and 0.5 L/h, respectively. After pre-
paration, NBW was used throughout the subsequent AD or HSAD pro-
cess.
2.3. Analytical methods
VS, TS, TAN and total nitrogen (TN) in the PM samples were mea-
sured based on the standard method (APHA, 2012). As little nitrite or
nitrate was detected in raw SM, total organic nitrogen (TON) was cal-
culated by subtracting TAN from TN. The biogas and methane yield, pH
and C/N ratio were determined according to the methods described in
the report (Fan et al., 2020). In this research, accumulative biogas yield
(mL/g-VS) and accumulative CH4 yield (mL/g-VS) were used to assess
AD process. Soluble carbohydrates and proteins were determined by
using the phenol–sulfuric method and Lowry method, respectively. The
alkalinity, including partial alkalinity (PA), intermediate alkalinity (IA)
and TA were tested according to the reported methods (Sun et al.,
2016). PA and TA were determined by an endpoint of pH 5.75 and 4.3,
respectively. IA was measured from pH 5.75 to 4.3. As for VFAs de-
termination, a GC-FID (GC-8A, SHIMADZU CO., Japan) was used. So-
luble total organic carbon (sTOC) was measured by using a TOC ana-
lyzer (TOC-VCSN, ASI-V autosampler, SHIMADZU CO., Japan).

2.4. Statistical analysis
For determination of NBW characterization and AD experiments,
mean values were calculated by adopting Microsoft Oﬃce Excel 2019
according to three parallel tests. For statistical analysis, one-way ana-
lysis of variance (ANOVA) was used. The signiﬁcant diﬀerence in this
study was set at p < 0.05.
3. Results and discussion
3.1. AD process stability
The pH value is the result of a combination of solubility equilibrium,
liquid–solid CO2 balance and acid-alkali balance during the AD process
(Chen et al., 2015). As shown in Fig. 1a, at the beginning of the AD
process, the pH value of all reactors dropped rapidly due to the large
amount of acid generation in the acidogenesis stages. The initial pH
values were diﬀerent because with the increase of TS, the content of PM
increased with the content of acidic substances increased. In addition,
the raw material PM had a low pH of 6.08 (Table 1), which indicated
that the raw material contained a large amount of acidic substances.
The pH value in R(8% TS)Control, R(10% TS)Control and R(10% TS)NBW
was maintained at around 6.3, indicating that the AD process of this
three kinds of reactors might be inhibited because of VFAs accumula-
tion (Fig. 1c). Other reactors, however, gradually increased after the
initial decline and remained at around 7.4 because VFAs ﬁnally con-
verted to methane (Fig. 1b, c and Fig. 3).
The VFAs concentration of R(3% TS)NBW and R(3% TS)Control de-
creased rapidly as the AD process progressed. When TS was about 3%,
the acetic acid was rapidly consumed and maintained at a lower level in
the later stage. Similarly, propionic and butyric acids were quickly
consumed in two weeks. Therefore, VFAs concentration and methane
production indicated acidogenesis and methanogenesis stages pro-
ceeded fairly well when TS content was about 3%. As TS content in-
creased, the initial VFAs concentration increased (Fig. 1b, c). When TS
content was about 6%, the initial VFAs concentration was about
5,500 mg/L. Compared with the R(6% TS)Control, R(6% TS)NBW ex-
perienced a faster increase rate in the initial stage and a faster con-
sumption rate in the later stage. As the TS content was further increased
to approximately 8%, the VFAs concentration in R(8% TS)Control was
accumulated and was not consumed in the later stage of HSAD. The R
(8% TS)NBW, however, was consumed in the late HSAD after the initial
accumulation. Regardless of R(10% TS)Control or R(10% TS)NBW, VFAs
concentration exceeded 10,000 mg/L after the 4th day, and they were
not consumed in the later stage of HSAD after the accumulation. The
most important phenomenon was that the pH value of R(8% TS)NBW
gradually increased after day 20. These results showed NBW addition
promoted the consumption of VFAs to covert methane, thereby re-
storing the stability of the AD system.
VFAs are related to alkalinity, pH and the activity of methanogens.
Therefore, they are important indicators for evaluating the performance
of AD processes (Abouelenien et al., 2014). In this work, the addition of
NBW played a role in promoting the consumption of VFAs leading to
maintain the stability of the HSAD system, avoiding serious inhibition
due to VFAs accumulation. This phenomenon led to promote the re-
covery of the pH value of the HSAD system for the stability. However,
when the concentration of VFAs was greater than the threshold, adding
NBW could not promote the fact that the HSAD process failed. This was
because the accumulation of VFAs leads to a decrease in pH value, and
when pH decreases, the toxicity of VFAs increases (Saady and Massé,
2015). Moreover, when pH value is low (5–7), VFAs are present in an
undissociated form, which is toxic for microorganisms and can speci-
ﬁcally aﬀect methanogens (Liew et al., 2011). In this work, when the
concentration of VFAs was greater than 10,000 mg/L, R(10% TS)NBW
could not be recovered in the late stage of HSAD (Fig. 1c). As for the pH
value of R(10% TS)NBW, it was about 6.3, which was in the range of 5–7
(Fig. 1a). In terms of the threshold that NBW could withstand the in-
hibition from VFAs, further researches are needed.
Changes in TA content in all reactors are shown in Fig. 1d. In the
late stage of AD, the TA content of RControl was signiﬁcantly lower than
that of RNBW when TS content was about 8% (Fig. 1d). However, in
other TS cases, there was no signiﬁcant diﬀerence between RControl and
RNBW. This indicated that when the HSAD system was slightly inhibited
(for example, R(8% TS)NBW), the addition of NBW could increase the TA
content, which was conducive to the restoration of the stability of the
HSAD system. However, when the HSAD system was severely sup-
pressed (such as R(10% TS)NBW), adding NBW had no signiﬁcant eﬀect
on TA content.
IA indicates the impact from VFAs while PA shows the available pH
buﬀering from ammonia and bicarbonate. Therefore, the IA/PA ratio
can be used to indicate the stability of the AD system. When IA/PA
suddenly increases, it indicates the pH buﬀering ability of AD decreases
(Sun et al., 2016). Fig. 2a shows the ratio between IA/PA under dif-
ferent TS content. As the AD process proceeded, the IA/PA ratio of R
(3% TS)NBW, R(3% TS)Control, R(6% TS)Control, R(6% TS)NBW and R(8%
TS)NBW was gradually decreasing. This showed that the stability of the
above ﬁve groups was better. Since the IA/PA ratio was in the range of
3 to 5.5 and was not decreased in R(8% TS)Control, R(10% TS)Control and
R(10% TS)NBW, these three kinds of reactors had the poor buﬀering
ability. The diﬀerent results of the IA/PA ratio of R(8% TS)NBW and R
(8% TS)Control indicated that NBW addition could improve the stability
of the HSAD system.
VFA/TA ratio is more reliable in detecting the stability of the AD
process than simply detecting the pH value (Chen et al., 2014). When

the ratio is lower than 0.4, the AD process is stable, which is the optimal
for AD process. When the ratio is higher than 0.8, the digester is prone
to signiﬁcant instability (Li et al., 2013). Fig. 2b shows the VFA/TA
ratio with or without NBW addition under diﬀerent TS content. Since
the VFA/TA ratio of R(8% TS)NBW was lower than 0.4 in the later stage
of HSAD, this indicated that the HSAD process of R(8% TS)NBW gra-
dually stabilized in the later stage. R(8% TS)Control, however, its ratio
was greater than 0.8, which indicated that R(8% TS)Contro did not return
to stability in the late stage of the HSAD process. Therefore, VFA/TA
ratio also showed that the addition of NBW improved the stability of
HSAD.
Both TAN and FAN are important factors inﬂuencing methanogenic
activity in the HSAD system. The TAN content of R(3% TS)Control, R(3%
TS)NBW, R(6% TS)Control, and R(6% TS)NBW did not exceed 1,500 mg/L
throughout the AD process (Fig. 2c). That is, when TS was 3% and 6%,
no ammonia inhibition occurred. When TS was about 8%, the TAN
content gradually increased as the AD process progressed. The TAN
content of R(8% TS)NBW was around 1,500 mg/L, while R(8% TS)Control
was continuously increased to about 2,000 mg/L. Chen et al. (2008)
reported that ammonia inhibition is possible when the TAN content
exceeds 1,700 mg/L. Therefore, when TS was 8%, ammonia inhibition
might occur in R(8% TS)NBW and R(8% TS)Control. The TAN content also
exceeded 1,500 mg/L when TS was about 10%, which indicated that
ammonia inhibition might also occur in R(10% TS)Control and R(10%
TS)NBW. FAN is capable of penetrating the cell membrane of micro-
organisms and accumulating inside the cell to cause proton imbalance
or toxic cytoplasmic enzymes. Therefore, FAN is more toxic than io-
nized ammonia (Niu et al., 2014). Except for R(6% TS)Control, R(6%
TS)NBW and R(8% TS)NBW, the FAN concentration of other digesters did
not exceed 50 mg/L throughout the AD process (Fig. 2d). Under the
same conditions of TAN and temperature, a change in pH value of 0.1
will result in a 25% change in FAN concentration (Chen et al., 2015).
Therefore, pH has a signiﬁcant impact on FAN. Since R(8% TS)Control, R
(10% TS)Control and R(10% TS)NBW had the lower pH (around 6.3), the
FAN content was also lower even though the TAN content was higher
than other digesters. The inhibition threshold for FAN concentrations is
reported to be 80–100 mg/L for conventional AD (De Baere et al.,
1984). Therefore, the inhibition from FAN did not occur in all digesters.
3.2. Methanogenesis and soluble organics performance

cess. When TS was 3% and 6%, the cumulative CH4 and biogas yields
from RControl were lower than those from RNBW. When TS was 8%, the
HSAD process of RControl was inhibited, and the biogas and CH4 pro-
duction were signiﬁcantly reduced. In contrast, RNBW was relatively
high with a TS of 8%, but its lag phase was relatively long compared to
the lower TS series. When TS was 10%, the HSAD process of RControl and

RNBW was suppressed, and biogas and CH4 yields were low. In terms of
cumulative biogas production (Fig. 3a), R(3% TS)NBW and R(6% TS)NBW
achieved 336 and 345 mL/g-VS, respectively, increasing by 17.5% and
23.9% in comparison to R(3% TS)Control and R(6% TS)Control, respec-
tively. R(8% TS)NBW obtained the highest biogas yield, which was
386 mL/g-VS. However, the corresponding R(8% TS)Control was only
62 mL/g-VS. This was due to that anaerobic bacteria, especially me-
thanogens, were reported to be sensitive under acidic environment and
their growth was inhibited in acidic conditions (Kothari et al., 2014).
The pH value of R(8% TS)Control was low (around 6.3), and VFAs in-
hibition occurred during the HSAD process (Fig. 1). As a result, the
activity of methanogens was aﬀected, and biogas production was re-
duced. For the cumulative CH4 production (Fig. 3b), R(3% TS)NBW and
R(6% TS)NBW reached 201 and 230 mL/g-VS, respectively, corre-
sponding to 20.3% and 25.0% increase when compared with R(3%
TS)Control and R(6% TS)Control, respectively. Similarly, R(8% TS)NBW
obtained the highest CH4 production, which was 261 mL/g-VS. R(8%
TS)Control, however, was only 23.8 mL/g-VS.
Previous reports showed the addition of NBW promote CH4 pro-
duction in AD process (Yang et al., 2019; Fan et al., 2020). In this study,
although the CH4 yield from RNBW was higher than RControl, it was still
lower than the theoretical methane potential from PM, which was 290
to 550 L-CH4/kg-organic matter (Ferreira et al., 2014). The reason
might be due to the presence of undegradable organics in PM, or it
might be due to the diﬀerence in the inoculum. In addition, in this
study, the methane increase rates of R(3% TS)NBW and R(6% TS)NBW
were 20.3% and 25.0%, respectively, which was lower than the 34%
methane increase rate achieved by low-temperature hydrothermal
pretreatment reported by Huang et al (2017). Simultaneously, when TS
content was greater than 10%, the eﬀect of NBW technology was also
inferior to the eﬀect achieved by using a down plug-ﬂow anaerobic
reactor (Chen et al. 2015). When anaerobic digestion was used to treat
animal manure with high TS, although the eﬀect of NBW was inferior to
low-temperature hydrothermal pretreatment technology and down
plug-ﬂow anaerobic reactor, NBW technology did not need to consume
too much energy, nor did it need to use complex reactor. Moreover, in
AD process, NBW technology also has advantages, especially low cost,
low pollution, and simple operation.
In this work, when TS was < 8%, the addition of NBW increased

reduce the degree of inhibition, which has been proven in the changing
trends of VFAs, pH, IA/PA ratio. When TS content was about 10%, the
HSAD process was severely inhibited, and NBW addition could not

Therefore, this work measured some soluble organics during AD
process. As shown in Fig. 4a, the soluble proteins in RNBW increased
rapidly and exceeded the corresponding RControl from the beginning to
the day 4. As the AD progressed, when TS was about 3% and 6%, the
soluble proteins were rapidly consumed in RNBW and RControl, possibly
due to the rapid reproduction of hydrolyzed bacteria during the early
stages of AD (Yuan et al., 2017). The soluble proteins in R(8% TS)NBW
dropped rapidly after day 20. However, R(8% TS)Control was not rapidly
consumed, which indicated inhibition has occurred and caused the
HSAD process to fail. When TS was about 10%, the soluble proteins of
RNBW and RControl were not consumed in a large amount, which also
showed that the HSAD process was not successful. In this work, the
changing trends of soluble proteins and carbohydrates during AD pro-
cess were basically similar (Fig. 4b). By analyzing soluble carbohy-
drates/proteins, it could be concluded that adding NBW could avoid the
accumulation of soluble organics when there was no serious inhibition
occurred in the HSAD process. However, when severe VFAs inhibition
occurred in R(10% TS)Control and R(10% TS)NBW, adding NBW could not
eﬀectively promote the consumption of soluble organics. When the TS
was 3% and 6%, both RNBW and RControl decreased rapidly ﬁrst and then
slowly decrease in VS content (Fig. 4c). The diﬀerence is that the VS
reduction rates in RControl on day 4 (9.8% in TS 3% and 3.6% in TS 6%)
were slower than those in RNBW (15.9% in TS 3% and 6.4% in TS 6%).
When TS was 8%, the VS reduction rates in RNBW was slower in the
early stage of AD, but it became faster in the later stage. As for the R(8%
TS)Control, however, the VS reduction rates were slow during the AD
process. Although the VS reduction rates of both R(10% TS)NBW and R
(10% TS)Control were slow, R(10% TS)NBW were still faster than that of
the R(10% TS)Control on day 4 (2.8% in RNBW and 1.9% in RControl).
However, with the further increase of VFAs content (Fig. 1c), the de-
crease of VS was no longer obvious when TS was about 10%. Therefore,
when the inhibition was not serious, the addition of NBW accelerates
the hydrolysis process, which has been reported (Yang et al., 2019).
However, when the HSAD process of R(10% TS)NBW was severely in-
hibited (excessive VFAs inhibition), adding NBW could not signiﬁcantly
increase the rate of hydrolysis in this study. Fig. 4d illustrates the
changes of sTOC throughout the AD process. Obviously, since there was
no ammonia inhibition and VFAs inhibition when TS was about 3% and
6%, the sTOC was ﬁrstly increased and then decreased. When TS was
8%, in the early stage, the sTOC of R(8% TS)NBW and R(8% TS)Control
accumulated continuously. With the HSAD progressed, the consump-
tion rates of sTOC from R(8% TS)NBW was higher than the accumulation
rates after a long lag phase, and the sTOC content gradually decreased.
R(8% TS)Control, however, was not rapidly consumed throughout the
HSAD process. When TS was 10%, the sTOC content in both R(10%
TS)NBW and R(10% TS)Control gradually stabilized after the initial in-
crease. The changes of sTOC content further illustrated that the HSAD
process of R(10% TS)NBW and R(10% TS)Control has been seriously in-
hibited. Meantime, when the inhibition was not serious in R(8% TS)NBW
and R(8% TS)Control, adding NBW could gradually alleviate the inhibi-
tion within a longer lag phase and promote the consumption of soluble
organics.
3.3. Related mechanisms
To clarify the relevant mechanisms, the characteristics of NBW were
analyzed in this work. Based on previous researches, CO2-NBW have
higher zeta potential, spin–spin relaxation times (T2), particle density
than DW (Wang et al., 2019, Wang et al., 2020). As known, zeta po-
tential has an important eﬀect on the stability of the bubble (Parmar
and Majumder, 2013). When zeta potential is high (negative or posi-
tive), colloids tend to avoid coalescence and have the property of being
electrically stable. Due to CO2-NBW addition, zeta potential from CO2-
NBW was signiﬁcantly higher than DW (p < 0.05). Therefore, CO2-
NBW addition may avoid the formation of aggregates in HSAD process.
T2 can be used to detect interactions between weak molecules such as
hydrogen bonding, steric eﬀects, and molecular mobility (Balci, 2005).
Liu et al (2013) pointed out that the number of nano-bubbles has a
positive correlation with the T2 in water and the introduction of nano-
bubbles can disturb the hydrogen-bonding network and make the water
molecules have higher mobility. In this work, the T2 value in CO2-NBW
was longer than that in DW, which indicated that the water molecules
in the reactors of RNBW have higher mobility than that of RControl. In
addition, NBW with higher mobility could improve nutrient mass
transfer eﬃciency from liquid to bacterial cells (Wang et al., 2019).
This may be beneﬁcial for improving the activity of microorganisms
and enzymes.

Fig. 6 describes the possible mechanisms of applying NBW in the
HSAD of SM. Unlike RControl, the reactors of RNBW contains not only raw
materials (PM and inoculum) and microorganisms but also large
amount of NBW particles with higher zeta potential (negative), T2 value
and electric conductivity than RControl. When PM is loaded into the
reactors of RNBW, NBW addition promotes the hydrolysis process of PM
to soluble organics by increasing the activity of hydrolytic enzymes. In
addition, NBW addition improves the mass transfer eﬃciency of nu-
trients from liquid to microbial cells and thus beneﬁcial to quickly in-
crease the activity of microorganisms. Meantime, NBW addition also
improves the mobility of water molecules. The improved mass transfer
eﬃciency of nutrients and the mobility of water molecules are con-
ducive to the consumption of soluble organics by microorganisms,
thereby accelerating the acidogenesis process and the production of
intermediate products, such as VFAs. When the content of the inter-
mediate products is lower than the threshold that NBW can withstand
the inhibition, AD or HSAD succeeds. NBW addition improves the sta-
bility of AD or HSAD process. Moreover, since NBW addition can pro-
mote the activity of methanogens, methane production is also im-
proved. However, when the content of the intermediate products is
higher than the threshold, NBW addition is not enough to change the

4. Conclusions
To reveal the eﬀect of NBW on HSAD of PM, this work evaluated the
digestion stability and methanogenesis performance of HSAD under
NBW addition. Results show that NBW addition improved the digestion
stability, buﬀered pH and alleviated the inhibitions caused by the ac-
cumulation of intermediate products (such as VFAs). NBW addition also
promoted the consumption of soluble proteins/carbohydrates. In ad-
dition, no matter in wet AD or HSAD process, methane production was
enhanced under NBW supplementation. Therefore, NBW-based HSAD
system is supposed to be capable of stable operation with increased
methane production, which still deserves further research.
